html:
The Middle Kingdom was the second great age of ancient Egypt, from about 2055 to 1650 BCE, after the country was reunited by Mentuhotep II. It followed the breakup of the Old Kingdom and the divided years of the First Intermediate Period.

Mentuhotep II was a ruler of Thebes in the south. He defeated the rival kings in the north and made Egypt one country again. The Twelfth Dynasty that followed was the heart of the period:

  • Amenemhat I moved the capital north to a new city near the Faiyum, and the kings drained and farmed that fertile basin.
  • Kings pushed south into Nubia and built a chain of great mud-brick forts along the Nile, facing the kingdom of Kerma.
  • Senusret III reduced the power of the provincial governors and was later honoured as a hero king.

Later Egyptians saw this as their classical age of writing. Its form of the language, Middle Egyptian, was studied by scribes for centuries, and works like the Story of Sinuhe were copied as models. Ordinary officials could now hope for an afterlife once reserved for kings, with spells written on their coffins.

In the Thirteenth Dynasty the kings grew weaker and changed often. People from the Levant settled in the delta, and their leaders, the Hyksos, took power there around 1650 BCE. Egypt split again until the kings of Thebes drove the Hyksos out and founded the New Kingdom.
sum: The Middle Kingdom was the second great age of ancient Egypt, from about 2055 to 1650 BCE, after the country was reunited by Mentuhotep II. It followed the breakup of the Old Kingdom and the divided years of the First Intermediate Period.
